children: Oil prices fell sharply Wednesday even after U.S. crude inventories declined, as the draw came in much smaller than Wall Street expected and gasoline and distillate stockpiles continued to build.
Commercial U.S. crude inventories fell by 600,000 barrels during the week ended September 11 to 423.4 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration.
That was slightly larger than the prior week's 400,000-barrel decline, but well below the 1.6 million-barrel draw economists had expected.
Crude oil futures dropped about 2.5% to $103.20 per barrel following the report.
The details underneath the headline crude draw were also relatively soft.

Gasoline inventories increased by 800,000 barrels after rising 1.3 million barrels the previous week. Distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, climbed another 1.6 million barrels following a 2.1 million-barrel build.
Those increases suggest refined-product supply remains comfortable even as headline crude stocks edge lower.
The Strategic Petroleum Reserve also declined, falling by 400,000 barrels to 285 million barrels from 285.4 million the prior week.

title: Oil Prices Send Fresh Signal After Surprise Inventory Data
